I have been working this land since I was seventeen. I know what these fields want. My sons go to the city to work, but they come back for wheat harvest and corn planting — I need to plan around that.

My 15 mu breaks down the way it always has: 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, 5 mu in cotton. Cotton prices have not been as good lately, but I know how to grow it and I am not going to change at my age.

For wheat I will use the same improved variety I have bought from the county cooperative for the past several years — it has not failed me. I put in base fertilizer before planting and come back with urea at jointing in spring. Three waterings: once before planting to get good emergence, once in early spring when the plants start growing again, and once at heading. Two pesticide rounds — one for weeds early on, one for aphids in May.

For maize I buy hybrid seed from the market in town — everyone does now, has been this way for twenty years. I sow it straight into the stubble after wheat comes off, no ploughing needed. I top-dress urea twice. Usually just two irrigations unless the summer is very dry.

Cotton is the hard work. My hands know it. I plough that ground deep in spring, plant seedlings, and then spend the summer managing it — watering, spraying for bollworm and whitefly, topping the plants. Five spray rounds at minimum. Without that it falls apart.
